newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds gain ground in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds gain ground in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities posted solid gains in thin trade on Thursday, mortgage experts said.
"The fact that (spreads) are not drastically wider, I'd have to say (mortgages) have done very well today," said one pass-through trader.
No major bid lists were spotted and trading volume was relatively thin, he said.
By late afternoon, yield spreads were unchanged to slightly tighter to Treasury paper.
Specifically, fixed-coupon pass-throughs were 3/32 to 9/32 higher overall, while comparable Treasuries were up 5/32 to 08/32.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was up 4/32 at 100-23/32, yielding 117 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper rose 9/32 to 100-27/32, and Freddie Mac issues were up 7/32 at 101 even.
Five-year Treasuries were up 5/32 at 6.74 percent, and 10-year notes were up 8/32 at 6.85 percent.

Despite Thursday's solid performance, market participants were still nervous about the future performance of mortgage paper, one Ginnie trader said. He explained that the nervousness stems from the market's fears of more interest rate hikes.
"But the worst case scenario is if we don't see any movement in any direction," the trader said.
